question: True or false: well-controlled trials show that music lessons make children better at maths and reading?
answer: False. Children who take lessons do score higher, but families who pay for lessons differ in many other ways. Giovanni Sala and Fernand Gobet pooled 54 studies: once trials assigned children at random and gave the comparison group another activity, the benefit fell to about zero. The violin teaches the violin.
move: Before crediting the activity, ask who chose to do it.
ask: Which good result in my life am I crediting to a habit, when it may come from my circumstances?
trap: Lesson-takers score higher, so the lessons must be raising the scores.
reference: Sala & Gobet, Cognitive and academic benefits of music training with children: A multilevel meta-analysis, Memory & Cognition, 2020
